chunks: Sahl, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and Ibn Sinan and Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Obedience to Ali is humility, and disobedience to him is disbelief in Allah.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how can obedience to Ali be humility and disobedience to him be disbelief in Allah?' So he replied: 'Indeed, Ali carries you upon the Truth; so if you obey him, you will be humbled, and if you disobey him, you will have disbelieved in Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of obedience to Imam Ali in Shia theology according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) elucidates the metaphysical status of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) as the embodiment of divine truth, where obedience to him is equated with humility (dhull) before God and disobedience with spiritual ruin (kufr). This narrative underscores the Shia doctrine of Wilayah, positioning Ali not merely as a political successor but as the essential conduit through which the community maintains its connection to the divine reality, a concept deeply rooted in the verse of Wilayah (4:59) and the call to follow the Messenger (3:31).

en.hubeali: H 14630 – Sahl, from Yahya Bin Al-Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabalat, from Is’haq Bin Ammaar, and Ibn Sinan, and Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws said:

‘The Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Obedience to Ali<sup>asws</sup> is humbleness and disobedience to him is blasphemy with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. It was said, ‘O Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, how can obedience to Ali<sup>asws</sup> be humbleness and disobedience to him<sup>asws</sup> be blasphemy with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> replied: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> carries you all upon the ‘الْحَقِّ’ Just, so if you obey him<sup>asws</sup> it would make you humble, and if you were to disobey him<sup>asws</sup>, you would have blasphemed against Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 182. Sahl, from Yahya Bin Al-Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabalat, from Is’haq Bin Ammaar, and Ibn Sinan, and Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: ‘

The Rasool Allah (saww) said: ‘Obedience to Ali (a.s.) is humbleness and disobedience to him is blasphemy with Allah (azwj)’. It was said, ‘O Rasool Allah (saww), how can obedience to Ali (a.s.) be humbleness and disobedience to him (a.s.) be blasphemy with Allah (azwj)?’ So he (saww) replied: ‘Ali (a.s.) carries you all upon the ‘الْحَقِّ’ Just, so if you obey him (a.s.) it would make you humble, and if you were to disobey him (a.s.), you would have blasphemed against Allah (azwj)’.
